name: a(n) is the maximum size of a subset S of {1, 2, ..., n} such that for any distinct elements t, u in S, t + u does not divide t*u.
comment: The set of all odd numbers in S gives a simple construction with density 1/2.
link: Sharvil Kesarwani, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..5000 (terms 1..84 from Yifan Xie).
Elijah Beregovsky, Equivalence of definitions of A005279, 2025.
P. Erdős and R. Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory, Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
formula: a(n) = a(n-1) + 1 for n in A174905. - _Elijah Beregovsky_, Nov 19 2025
example: For n = 6, the set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} satisfies the condition. In the other direction, we cannot have {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} since 3 + 6 divides 3*6, so a(6) = 5.
author: _Yifan Xie_, Sep 07 2025
